# Dealing a hand (and fixing mistakes)

*How to shuffle, deal and burn like a pro, plus what to do when a card is exposed or someone gets the wrong number of cards.*

3 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

In most home games the deal rotates with the button, so everyone deals sooner or later. A clean deal keeps the game fast and avoids arguments. You don’t need fancy shuffles — just a consistent routine.

## Shuffle

- Keep the cards low and face down so nobody glimpses the bottom card.
- **Riffle shuffle several times**, then cut. Four riffles is the usual minimum; seven mix a deck thoroughly.
- Offer the cut to the player on your right, or cut yourself onto a cut card.
- With two decks, the next dealer shuffles the spare deck while you deal.

## Deal

1. Check the blinds are posted.
2. Starting with the small blind, deal **one card at a time** clockwise, until everyone has two (four in Omaha). The button gets the last card.
3. Keep the cards low and slide them across the felt; don’t flip them in the air.
4. Wait until preflop betting is over before touching the deck again.

## Burn and turn

Before each round of community cards, **burn** the top card face down, then deal the new cards face up:

| Round | Burn | Deal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flop | 1 card | 3 cards |
| Turn | 1 card | 1 card |
| River | 1 card | 1 card |

Burn cards protect against marked cards and accidental glimpses of the top card. Keep them separate from the discards in case you need to reconstruct the deck after a mistake.

## When something goes wrong

| Problem | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The first or second card of the deal is exposed | Misdeal: gather the cards, reshuffle and deal again |
| A later hole card is exposed by the dealer | Finish the deal, then give that player the top card of the deck as a replacement; the exposed card becomes the first burn card |
| Two or more hole cards exposed | Misdeal |
| A player got too many or too few cards | Misdeal, as long as no betting has happened yet |
| A player exposes their own card | Their problem — the hand goes on |
| The flop is dealt before betting finished | Put the flop aside, finish the betting, reshuffle those cards into the deck and deal a new flop without a new burn |
| A card is found face up in the deck | Put it aside and carry on with the next card |

> **Note — Misdeal ≠ new blinds:** After a misdeal, the button stays where it was and the same blinds are used for the redeal.

## Dealer habits worth copying

- Announce the pot size when asked — and in pot-limit, when someone wants to bet the pot.
- Push the pot to the winner only after the hands have been read.
- Say “action is on you” when someone hasn’t noticed it’s their turn.
- If you’re playing the hand you’re dealing, take your time — dealing isn’t a reason to rush your own decisions.
